clue.text: Officer's co-worker decorated in famous Venetian building at last

indicators.note: the word for decorated is placed in the middle of the Venetian's name

parts.note: Marco Polo, the explorer, was Venice's most famous son
a cake decorated with icing is iced

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word building is used

explanation.surface: A tourist's note about some officer's companion being honoured inside a celebrated Venetian landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Famous Venetian building' reads as one phrase, like the Doge's Palace, but the Venetian is Marco POLO, with ICED put 'in' him and the G from 'at last' of building.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer's canine partner is a trained dog working alongside the handler on patrols.

clue.text: People, as ever, welcoming polite word

indicators.note: the opening words take in, or welcome, the answer within their run of letters

explanation.surface: Folk, as always, greet others with a courteous word.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'peoPLE AS Ever', taken in by 'welcoming'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the standard courtesy added to a request, the magic word children are taught to say.

clue.text: Larkin and colleagues tease liars in bar

indicators.note: to tease wool or hair is to pull it apart and loosen it, so these letters are disentangled and rearranged

explanation.surface: The poet Larkin and friends mock the fibbers propping up the pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: Philip Larkin, the English poet, worked for decades as university librarian at Hull, so he is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkin ran a university library, so he and his professional colleagues are keepers of book collections.

clue.text: Perhaps hare after eccentric old maid?

indicators.note: the hunted-animals word comes after the eccentric-person word

parts.note: a card is an old-fashioned word for an odd, amusing character
hare is an example of game, animals hunted for sport and food

explanation.surface: Is the hare chasing behind some batty elderly spinster?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old maid' looks like a person tied to 'eccentric', but it is the children's card game of that name; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Maid is a children's pastime played with a pack, where the loser is left holding the odd queen.

clue.text: Policeman seizing stolen loincloth

indicators.note: the policeman takes hold of, and so contains, the word for stolen

parts.note: DI is short for Detective Inspector
stolen goods are hot

explanation.surface: An officer confiscates a pilfered loincloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the loincloth worn by men in India.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the long cloth wrapped round the waist and legs, traditional menswear in India.

clue.text: Feed a friend too much salt

parts.note: to glut is to feed too much, the sense spread over 'Feed' and 'too much'
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Overfeeding a pal with salt, a warning about diet.
explanation.walkthrough: GLUT means 'feed too much', its sense split around 'a friend'. The answer is a salt of glutamic acid, as in monosodium glutamate.
explanation.definitionFit: Monosodium glutamate, the flavour enhancer, is a sodium salt of glutamic acid, hence a chemical salt.

clue.text: Hit piece of furniture, gathering dust

indicators.note: the furniture word gathers the dust word into its middle

parts.note: a bed is a piece of furniture
ash is the dusty residue of burning

explanation.surface: Someone thumps a neglected cabinet that has been collecting dust.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe striking something hard, so they are synonyms in the past tense.

clue.text: Rebecca's son oddly ignoring new status

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters of the phrase are passed over, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Rebecca's boy strangely snubs his newly acquired standing.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters of NEW STATUS to keep E, S, A, U. In Genesis, Rebecca bore twins, Jacob and his elder brother.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Rebecca (Rebekah) and Isaac had twin boys, the hairy elder selling his birthright to Jacob.

clue.text: The setter writes to support worker, contrary sort

indicators.note: in a down answer the following letters sit beneath the worker, holding it up

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker
the setter refers to himself as I
to type is to write on a keyboard

explanation.surface: The compiler describes typing up praise for a labourer, then calls the result an awkward opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an opposite or contrasting type, so a contrary kind of thing.

clue.text: Secret affair left couple holding a child

indicators.note: the numeral pair holds the A between its letters

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
a son is a child

explanation.surface: An illicit fling left two people bringing up a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' looks like the lovers, but it is just II, Roman two.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is used for an illicit romantic or sexual relationship kept hidden from others.

clue.text: Organise AGM, or be subject to ban

indicators.note: the letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Arrange the annual general meeting or face a prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an official prohibition, especially on trade with a particular country.

clue.text: Alluring female is short of shilling after time

indicators.note: the shortened word follows the time word

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

indicators.note: the word is is left lacking the letter for shilling

parts.note: S was the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin

explanation.surface: A seductive woman is penniless after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated S. A houri is one of the beautiful maidens of the Islamic paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a nymph of the Muslim paradise, the word came to mean any voluptuously beautiful woman.

clue.text: Working girl has an ideal place to live

indicators.note: the letters are worked over into a new shape

explanation.surface: A young woman with a job has found her dream home.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the hidden paradise valley in James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon, it means an earthly utopia.

clue.text: Humility means transcending yourself, primarily

parts.note: modes are means or methods

indicators.note: the leading letters of the following two words are taken

explanation.surface: A self-help line: true humbleness means rising above your ego.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a lack of vanity, an unassuming estimate of one's own merits, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Condemned English art, laying it on thick

indicators.note: condemned buildings are wrecked, so these letters are demolished and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A critic panning English painting, perhaps with exaggerated flattery for something else.
explanation.definitionFit: To slather is to spread something thickly and lavishly, so the participle describes plastering it on heavily.

clue.text: Adjutant returned after month for papers etc

indicators.note: the turned word follows the month letter
the assistant word is read backwards

parts.note: an adjutant is a military aide

explanation.surface: A military assistant came back after a month away to collect newspapers and the like.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers, broadcasters and other outlets are collectively the press and its kin, the means of mass communication.

clue.text: One shunning less stylish nursing sister in Oz?

indicators.note: the trimmed word holds the sister inside it as if cradling her
the word for less stylish avoids, so loses, the letter for one

parts.note: dowdier means more frumpy, less stylish
I is the Roman numeral one
a nun is a religious sister

explanation.surface: A frumpy nurse in Australia keeps herself to herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nursing sister' tempts as one phrase, but 'nursing' signals the insertion, made after 'shunning' drops I. The question mark flags Oz as slang for Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is colloquially referred to as lying at the bottom of the globe, so in Oz is an idiomatic match.

clue.text: Sheepish male with drug, pursuing fine physique

indicators.note: the sheep-and-drug letters follow the letter for fine

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a ram is a male sheep
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A shy man on drugs chasing a great body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' reads as shy but literally means 'of sheep'.
explanation.definitionFit: Frame describes a person's bodily build, so it is a synonym for physique.

clue.text: Wretched old bird

parts.note: flaming is a mild British curse word meaning damned or wretched

explanation.surface: A grumble about some miserable aged bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The pink wading bird with long legs and a bent bill is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Division of gas producer changing hands

indicators.note: left is swapped for right, so the L becomes an R

parts.note: shale rock yields shale gas through fracking

explanation.surface: Part of an energy company is sold to new owners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing hands' looks like a sale but swaps L (left hand) for R (right hand).
explanation.definitionFit: A portion handed out or split off from a whole is one's part, so it is a division.

clue.text: Leave gym with initially accelerated pulse

parts.note: to split is slang for to leave
PE, physical education, is school gym

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Someone quits the gym once their heart rate has shot up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat, but here it means a dried edible seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are dried leguminous seeds such as lentils, peas and beans, so this dried halved pea is one.

clue.text: Give birth with anguished cry?

parts.note: help is what someone cries out in distress

explanation.surface: Bringing a baby into the world accompanied by a scream of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb is used of dogs and other animals producing young, so it means to give birth.

clue.text: Don't drink tar and varnish!

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, as is an AB, able seaman
a stain is a coloured varnish for wood

explanation.surface: A warning label: do not swallow the wood treatment!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' looks like the black goo, a fair partner for varnish, but it is old slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain from alcohol is the core sense of the verb, as in staying teetotal.

clue.text: Ethereal and extremely attractive hideaway seen from the south

indicators.note: only the end letters of the word attractive are taken
in a down answer, reading from the bottom upward turns the den word backwards

parts.note: a lair is an animal's hideaway

explanation.surface: A dreamy, beautiful retreat glimpsed from below.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something airy and insubstantial, light as the upper air.

clue.text: Perhaps Dorothy's served up heavy food

indicators.note: in a down answer the pieces are turned upward, read bottom to top

parts.note: EG, for example, means perhaps
Dot is short for Dorothy, so Dorothy's is Dot's

explanation.surface: Maybe it's Dorothy who dishes up a stomach-filling meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Write EG DOTS and turn it upward with 'served up'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names thick, starchy, filling food such as suet puddings, the stuff of school dinners.

clue.text: Most unjust if nature's destroyed

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An environmentalist's cry: the cruellest outcome would be wrecking the natural world.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the superlative of a word meaning unjust, so the most inequitable.

clue.text: Head of Finance sped about Swiss capital

indicators.note: only the first letter of Finance is taken

parts.note: ran means sped
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: The finance chief zoomed around Bern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swiss capital' wants to be Bern; it means Swiss money.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of Switzerland is this unit, so it is Swiss capital in the sense of money.

clue.text: Run home with rogue

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a cur is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A villain makes a dash back to base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' as in running up a bill or running a risk.
explanation.definitionFit: One runs up debts or runs risks, which is to bring them on oneself; the verbs are synonyms there.

clue.text: Leaves hotel for club

parts.note: cos is a lettuce, a vegetable of leaves
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A gardener walks out of the hotel and heads for the golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb but is cos lettuce; a cosh is a British word for a short heavy truncheon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosh is a short, heavy bludgeon, so it is a kind of club used as a weapon.

clue.text: Turned to use backless cooker, perhaps explosive

indicators.note: the fruit loses its final letter

parts.note: a cooker is a cooking apple, here an example of the fruit
IED stands for improvised explosive device

explanation.surface: A kitchen hazard: an oven with no back panel might blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooker' is not an oven but a cooking apple, Bramley being the classic British one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put into practical use has been brought to bear, so used in practice.

clue.text: Develop case of gangrene, say

indicators.note: the outer letters of gangrene form its casing

parts.note: to state is to say

explanation.surface: Claim to have contracted a bout of gangrene.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry and grow young in the womb is to develop them, and ideas can be developed the same way.

clue.text: Figure on plane reportedly demolished fish

indicators.note: the two words are said out loud and heard as one

parts.note: demolished is wrecked and fish is angle, the verb meaning to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: An airborne passenger's story about a smashed-up fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aircraft, but it is a flat geometric plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-sided shape with right angles is a figure drawn in plane geometry.
